guide.description: A few simple habits for a thoughtful club workflow.
guide.student_body: Open your classroom and choose an assignment or join a live session. Read the problem carefully. Write your reasoning or source code, attach handwritten work if needed, and submit. A saved draft is not a submission. Return to Submissions & review for released feedback. In team workspaces, compare conflicting edits instead of overwriting a teammate. Competitions are individual and close on the server deadline.
guide.teacher_body: Create a classroom, invite students, and add your own or licensed problems. Enter Russian, English, or both. Create an assignment, session, or competition with fixed problem snapshots and scoring criteria. Publish assignments; start sessions and release each problem. Review submitted work and explicitly release feedback. Form teams around specific tasks and monitor their saved revisions. End a competition, review every attempt, then publish results.
guide.admin_body: Invite teachers, manage account access, and enroll existing students into classrooms. Send invitation links privately. Collect only the name and school email needed for participation. Agree on retention and access policies with your school before using real student records. Account recovery is handled by a trusted server operator.
guide.saving_body: Wait for the Saved label before closing a tab. Unsaved recovery text stays only in this browser tab and is removed on sign-out. Downloads may remain on shared computers: remove them when finished. Never upload confidential information into a problem statement or a classroom-wide resource. The platform does not run student code or use AI services.
